gen-gf-gugi-gf-narnoor: Gugi has a pencil-line consistency, with tall lowercase that nearly climbs to the capitals. Narnoor, a plain sans with short ascenders over big bowls, is the quieter partner and simply gets on with the text.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-display: Bold, bendy, a bit cheeky: Gugi draws its round letters like bent wire. And Noto Sans Display, a sans-serif with a big, tall middle zone, would swallow that heading's personality if Gugi were made small.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-play: Gugi's curves hold a pencil-line consistency from start to finish. It excels at striking, open-ended display letters, while Play, a plain sans with a faint letterpress-slug shift between thick and thin, excels at staying out of the way.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-port-lligat-sans: Gugi draws a rope-thin outline with no thick or thin parts. Port Lligat Sans, a sans with unfinished bowls and tightly packed characters, would crowd the page if the heading were shrunk down beside it.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-ramabhadra: Ramabhadra, a sans with a prominent x-height, handles the running text with a clean, businesslike manner. Gugi, meanwhile, owns the loud moments, its curves carrying the heft of a rope's body.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-rambla: Distinctive is the right word for Gugi, whose tube-like strokes hold their thickness through every bend. And Rambla, a sans with small letters standing almost as tall as capitals, only earns that heading its keep when Gugi goes big and short.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-recursive: Approachable and modern, Recursive keeps its thickness constant in every direction under a tall mean line. And Gugi, with open terminals and curves that match its stems, supplies the bolder voice above it.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-roboto-condensed: Roboto Condensed reads tight, with barely visible gaps inside each word and a line that glides under the eye like wire. Gugi does its best work as a bold, open-terminalled headline, while Roboto Condensed does its best work carrying a sans-serif's enlarged lowercase body.
